definition: A warning, limitation, or qualifying statement attached to a scientific claim or experimental interpretation.
manuscriptExample: A notable caveat of this organoid model is the absence of a vascularized stromal microenvironment.
conferenceExample: During the editorial meeting, we emphasized this caveat so the authors do not overstate their clinical findings.

definition: To confirm, support, or give additional authority to a dataset using independent evidence.
etymology: From Latin corroboratus, past participle of corroborare ('to strengthen').
manuscriptExample: Orthogonal qPCR analysis corroborated the micro-RNA microarray findings across all primary biopsies.
conferenceExample: The external referee requested additional mass spectrometry assays to corroborate co-immunoprecipitation results.

definition: Naturally accompanying, co-occurring, or associated with another physiological event.
etymology: From Late Latin concomitans, present participle of concomitari ('to accompany').
manuscriptExample: Inhibition of CDK4/6 induced senescence with a concomitant reduction in phosphorylated Rb protein levels.
conferenceExample: We discussed whether the concomitant spike in liver enzymes was drug-induced or vehicle-related.
